clusters.name: Your stepfather Desmond joining the household, 1987
clusters.reason: Around 1987 when you were settling into secondary school: your distance from Desmond, your closeness to your father, your stepmother's separation from him over a baby, and your anxiety about making the city chess squad all fall together in those months. Your grandfather's gambling and your mother's harsh memories of him sit outside this time.

clusters.name: Your grandfather Gordon's death, 1991–1992
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather's stroke in June 1991 and through the following year: your late nights and your wrist injury that stopped your playing, the blow-up with Rafe and your slide into getting high and fixing radios, your low and lost functioning, and your mother's wedding to Desmond all fell within these months. Your grandfather's death sits among them as the family shifted. Your father's father came back into the family a couple of years before; the rebuild of Hollin Road and the move there happened as these troubles were building.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Winifred's bowel cancer and death, 2001–2004
clusters.reason: Around 2001 and 2002 when your grandmother was found to have bowel cancer, your own performing ran out of steam, you had a disastrous audition, and you grew distant from your family and friends; you left Thornbury for Gull Harbour, met Marisol there, moved in with her, then split and sank into deep depression once you returned. You could not face your parents, but relied on friends—Corbin, Silas, Hamish—through those months. Your grandmother spent her final months in your parents' home, and you visited her hung over on your way to the airport. She died in February 2004. The distance you felt from family, the closeness you found with friends, and the slow recovery you began with your therapist Victor all sat alongside her illness and death.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Lorna's death and your nursing school move, 2008
clusters.reason: Around early 2008 when your grandmother died and you moved to nursing school in Marlow Sound: your mother pressed you to visit while you were at the lodge with Silas, you kept the door shut on her, then stopped speaking to her when you left for school that summer. Your aunt Imogen had a stroke around the same time. The silence between you and your mother held for roughly a year; you were too drained for conversation at the lodge, and contact cost too much once you had moved. These months turned the way you and your mother stayed in touch.

clusters.name: Your marriage to Wren and her family's closeness, 2017–2019
clusters.reason: Around your wedding to Wren in March 2017 and through the following two years: your contact with your mother eased off, your sister's life shifted with her marriage and pregnancy, your cousin Alice's illness came to light, and your aunt Imogen's confusion grew worse. Wren's mother's retirement party in October 2019 brought her whole family together at the lake house, where you felt you did not belong and your sleep shattered; you felt swamped by the back-and-forth of the season, you were overfunctioning to settle Wren when she was swamped, and your sleep troubles sat at their worst around her family. Your job had steadied and paid well, yet your anxiety about driving projects forward stayed high. You took a sleeping pill to stop fretting about sleep itself. Your sister was expecting her first child. The strains were in how you and Wren's family held together, and in how your own family's troubles piled up around you.
